gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Epoch 12105A-H heater starts with only 0.5 A of incoming charge current. That is far below the 10 A LiTime's heated Group 24 needs in Regular mode and the more than 4 A per battery Renogy's Pro heater needs, so it decides whether a weak winter source (a small solar controller or a trickle charger) can warm each battery at all.
standout_why: I compared against CompareFoundry (cited), BatteryTrail spec database (cited) and BoondockMaps (cited). CompareFoundry gives LiTime's 10 A heater minimum and Renogy's 4 A minimum. BatteryTrail gives Renogy's 4 A per battery and its parallel-only limit. Neither gives a heater start current for Epoch, the battery ChatGPT picked as best overall. BoondockMaps says Epoch is heated to -4°F but nothing about what turns the heater on, and nothing on series or parallel wiring. I could not read Gear Ranking (cited): WebFetch hit a self-signed-certificate error and the curl fallback needed approval. So I can't rule out that it states the Epoch 0.5 A figure, which is why this is a 2 and not a 3.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's Epoch pick for anyone charging in the cold from a low-current source: Epoch says its heater runs from 0.5 A of charger current, while LiTime's Regular mode needs a charger of at least 10 A and Renogy's Pro heater needs more than 4 A reaching each battery. Wiring also separates them: Epoch allows up to 4 in series and 4 in parallel (48 V, 420 Ah), while Renogy's self-heating Pro is parallel-only, up to 8, so it cannot be built into a 24 V or 48 V bank. The page should give each heated pick a line saying 'heater needs ≥X A from the charger' and another for 'series/parallel limit'.

findings.label: Heater start condition
findings.value: A connected charger supplying at least 0.5 A. The heater runs on incoming charge current only, never on stored battery energy.
findings.source_title: 12V 105Ah Heated & Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery – Epoch Batteries
findings.note: Quoted from Epoch's US product page: 'Charger connected and supplying at least 0.5A; powered by incoming charge current only, never stored battery energy.'

findings.label: Cold charge cutoff and resume
findings.value: Charging is disabled below 0°C (32°F) and resumes automatically at 5°C (41°F). The heating system is tested to -20°C (-4°F).
findings.source_title: 12V 105Ah Heated & Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery – Epoch Batteries

findings.label: Series/parallel limit
findings.value: Up to 4 in series and 4 in parallel (4S4P): 48 V in series, 420 Ah in parallel
findings.source_title: 12V 105Ah Heated & Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery – Epoch Batteries
findings.note: Quoted: 'Max (4) in Series, Max (4) in Parallel - 4S4P.' 420 Ah = 4 × 105 Ah.

findings.label: Charge sources Epoch approves
findings.value: A LiFePO4-compatible charger, RV converter, solar charge controller, inverter charger or DC-to-DC charger, set to Epoch's recommended charging parameters. The only communication the page describes is Bluetooth to the Epoch Li-Ion app, and it names no Victron or other closed-loop pairing.
findings.source_title: 12V 105Ah Heated & Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery – Epoch Batteries
findings.note: The page links a user manual, data sheet and spec sheet (cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0251/0484/2798/...). I opened the data sheet but its text was compressed and unreadable.

findings.source_title: 12V 105Ah Heated & Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery – Epoch Batteries

findings.label: Warranty terms
findings.value: Free replacement in years 1–3, then 40% off MSRP for a replacement in years 4–11. Registration requested within 90 days, or keep proof of purchase.
findings.source_title: 12V 105Ah Heated & Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery – Epoch Batteries

findings.label: Heater start condition
findings.value: In Regular mode it needs a charger of at least 10 A. Energy-efficient mode can heat from the battery's own power when state of charge is above 20%. It heats between -20°C and 5°C.
findings.source_title: Choose a 12V LiFePO4 battery: capacity, BMS limits, cold charging and US packages – CompareFoundry
findings.note: Figure as given by CompareFoundry. LiTime's own product page returned HTTP 429 twice, so I could not check it against the maker.

findings.label: Heater start condition
findings.value: The heater runs only with more than 4 A of charge current per battery, from -4°F to 41°F
findings.source_title: LiFePO4 RV Battery Spec Database: Complete Comparison (All Major Brands) – BatteryTrail
findings.note: BatteryTrail: 'The heater only runs when the charger supplies more than 4A per battery.' CompareFoundry says the same: 'only when a stable charge current above 4 A is present.' Arithmetic: a 2-battery parallel bank needs more than 8 A total if the current splits evenly.

findings.label: Series/parallel limit
findings.value: Parallel only, up to 8 batteries. No series, so it cannot make a 24 V or 48 V bank.
findings.source_title: LiFePO4 RV Battery Spec Database: Complete Comparison (All Major Brands) – BatteryTrail
findings.note: CompareFoundry says the same: 'Renogy documents parallel only, up to 8.' It also gives a charge cutoff of 32°F, resuming at 37°F, citing Renogy's manual.
